briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 15, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Disasters and Deepening Water Crisis
sections.content: News collected today warns of the global intensification of extreme disasters caused by climate change. In particular, a series of research findings have been released, indicating that El Niño, climate change, and specifically global warming, have had a greater impact on the intensification of Hurricane 'Polo' [170, 177, 180, 185, 186, 187]. Domestically, the CEO of Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-water) has attributed the decrease in hydropower generation at Unmun Dam to climate change and announced plans to explore water level adjustments [1, 38], and concerns have been raised that climate change phenomena, such as the floods in Nepal, could also affect our region [43]. Internationally, water scarcity and extreme weather events are spreading across the board, including increased wildfire risks due to weakening Santa Ana winds in Southern California [169], a surge in wildfires in the Brazilian Amazon [181, 189], and severe drought declared in six regions of England, threatening public water supply [193]. In Afghanistan, a tragic situation has arisen where families are forced to sell young girls into marriage due to drought [194], demonstrating how the climate crisis is leading to humanitarian disasters [175].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts, Achievements, and Challenges
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are underway to achieve carbon neutrality. Seventeen regional carbon neutrality support centers nationwide have launched a council to strengthen policy cooperation for local greenhouse gas reduction [11, 65, 71, 73, 76, 94, 100, 103], and various local governments, including Goyang, Osan, and Yangsan cities, are expanding greenhouse gas reduction target settings, implementing community-based carbon neutrality policies, and enhancing environmental education for citizens [5, 31, 36, 44, 47, 55, 57, 58, 59, 68, 91, 95, 102, 104, 106, 111, 114]. Furthermore, carbon neutrality ideas from future generations are being piloted in real-world settings [60, 70, 93, 113], and participation from industry and academia is active, including the promotion of carbon-reducing concrete credit certification [61, 87], forest carbon neutrality practices [74, 96, 97, 123], and technology development in the aerospace sector [82]. However, criticisms are also being raised that some efforts are merely superficial or lack substantial impact, such as the insufficient performance of the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute's (KEITI) carbon neutrality promotion projects [63, 77] or the controversy surrounding Samsung Card's 'illusion' of carbon neutrality [112], indicating a lack of practical effectiveness [67, 79, 90, 92, 122].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Change Adaptation and Agricultural Innovation Trends
sections.content: Efforts to adapt to the impacts of climate change and strengthen resilience are also actively underway across various regions in Korea. The Korea National Arboretum is discussing directions for innovating its research organization to respond to climate change and AI [2], while Sangju and Pohang cities have conducted research services and field evaluations for crop development plans and rice variety discovery in preparation for climate change [4, 19, 23, 48, 49]. In particular, Jinan County is promoting the cultivation of high-income fruit trees, including establishing a 'premium domestic apple complex' in response to climate change [7, 37], and the 'Saechungmu' rice variety, which withstands heatwaves and heavy rainfall well, has confirmed its quality competitiveness [6, 56]. Furthermore, Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) and the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) are strengthening cooperation in developing convergence technologies for predicting weather variability and improving renewable energy efficiency to address the issue of 'weather-sensitive power grids' [15, 127, 133, 139, 143, 148, 157], which is expected to contribute to climate crisis adaptation and infrastructure stabilization. Chungcheongbuk-do Province has published a climate crisis response policy guide 'ADAPT' to help citizens understand the issues [39, 45, 109], and adaptation efforts through education are also expanding, with programs at the Yongin Climate Change Experience Education Center being designated as excellent environmental education [24, 33].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Partnerships and Corporate Climate Action
sections.content: Domestic companies' overseas climate change response support projects are bearing fruit and positively impacting the international community. Hyundai Engineering has successfully concluded a three-year climate change response support project in Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam, transferring related infrastructure, including an education center and tree planting sites, to local institutions [3, 8, 9, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 25, 26, 28, 29, 30, 32, 34, 35, 40, 41, 46, 51, 52, 54, 191]. These efforts contribute to strengthening Vietnam's climate change adaptation capabilities and are recognized as exemplary cases of Korean companies' ESG management and global social contribution. Furthermore, international discussions on climate action are actively progressing, with Turkey preparing regional climate action projects in anticipation of the COP31 Climate Change Conference [190].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Policy Discussions
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is being addressed as a crucial agenda both domestically and internationally, with technology development and market expansion accelerating. SK Oceanplant is accelerating its penetration into the offshore wind power market by participating in Taiwan's largest renewable energy exhibition in the Asia-Pacific region [126, 131, 135, 137, 141, 146, 150, 152, 161], and the global renewable energy market is expected to grow, with Italy's solar power generation capacity projected to reach up to 136.7 GW by 2040 [138]. Domestically, Chungcheongbuk-do Province is concretizing its 'Chungbuk-type RE100' strategy, linking renewable energy with industrial demand [136, 142], and Saemangeum is expanding its renewable energy projects, including 'rooftop solar,' in conjunction with the AI and semiconductor industries, to become a 'practical RE100 hub' [158]. However, challenges requiring policy improvements and support abound, such as the downward adjustment of Seoul's 2030 renewable energy target [128], calls for a national master plan to address the sluggish development of renewable energy in rural and fishing communities [129, 140, 156], and regional imbalances in offshore wind farm usage fees [167], among other issues requiring policy improvements and support [162, 165].

briefing.closing: This concludes the climate briefing for October 15, 2026. We look forward to seeing you again at the next briefing.

articles.description: The closest land price is the standard. In the West and South Seas with many islands, lower land prices are applied. The Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) submitted 75 cases of 'local regulations' for improvement. Local businesses have poured in requests to amend regulations that do not align with reality, such as offshore wind usage fees differing by tens of times depending on the presence or absence of islands in the same sea area.
